securityAssessment.summary: The authentication system has several critical security vulnerabilities that must be addressed before enterprise deployment.

criticalVulnerabilities.title: Insecure Token Storage in localStorage
criticalVulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-922: Insecure Storage of Sensitive Information
criticalVulnerabilities.description: JWT tokens and refresh tokens are stored in localStorage, making them vulnerable to XSS attacks. localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript code, including malicious scripts.
criticalVulnerabilities.impact: Complete session hijacking, unauthorized access to all user data and Kubernetes cluster management capabilities
criticalVulnerabilities.exploitability: HIGH - Any XSS vulnerability can steal tokens
criticalVulnerabilities.attackScenario:
1. Attacker injects malicious script via XSS
2. Script reads localStorage.getItem('authToken')
3. Attacker gains full authentication access
4. Tokens persist across browser sessions
criticalVulnerabilities.remediation: Implement httpOnly cookies with SameSite=Strict and Secure flags. Remove all localStorage token storage.

criticalVulnerabilities.title: Missing CSRF Protection
criticalVulnerabilities.description: No CSRF protection mechanisms are implemented. All API requests are vulnerable to CSRF attacks.
criticalVulnerabilities.impact: Unauthorized actions performed on behalf of authenticated users, including cluster modifications and GPIO control
criticalVulnerabilities.exploitability: HIGH - Simple HTML forms can trigger actions
criticalVulnerabilities.attackScenario:
1. User visits malicious website while logged in
2. Site sends hidden POST request to pi-controller API
3. Browser automatically includes authentication
4. Unauthorized actions executed
criticalVulnerabilities.remediation: Implement CSRF tokens for all state-changing operations. Use SameSite cookie attributes.

criticalVulnerabilities.title: Automatic Token Refresh Without User Consent
criticalVulnerabilities.description: Tokens are automatically refreshed without user interaction, potentially extending compromised sessions indefinitely.
criticalVulnerabilities.impact: Stolen tokens remain valid for extended periods, increasing exposure window
criticalVulnerabilities.attackScenario:
1. Attacker steals access token
2. Before token expires, automatic refresh extends session
3. Attacker maintains persistent access
4. User unaware of compromise
criticalVulnerabilities.remediation: Require user interaction for session extension. Implement sliding window with absolute maximum session time.

highVulnerabilities.title: Missing Security Headers
highVulnerabilities.description: Critical security headers are missing: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options
highVulnerabilities.impact: Increased XSS risk, clickjacking vulnerabilities, MIME-type confusion attacks
highVulnerabilities.attackScenario:
1. Missing CSP allows inline scripts
2. XSS payload executes
3. Missing X-Frame-Options allows clickjacking
4. HTTPS downgrade attacks possible
highVulnerabilities.remediation: Configure comprehensive security headers in server/proxy configuration

highVulnerabilities.title: Insufficient Session Timeout Implementation
highVulnerabilities.description: Session extension mechanism uses window.location.reload() which is unreliable and doesn't properly validate session extension
highVulnerabilities.impact: Sessions may not properly expire, indefinite session persistence possible
highVulnerabilities.attackScenario:
1. User clicks 'Extend Session'
2. Page reload may fail silently
3. User believes session extended but tokens expired
4. Inconsistent security state
highVulnerabilities.remediation: Implement proper token refresh API call with error handling

highVulnerabilities.title: Sensitive Data Exposure in Error Messages
highVulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through Error Messages
highVulnerabilities.description: Authentication errors may expose sensitive information about system internals
highVulnerabilities.impact: Information disclosure that aids further attacks
highVulnerabilities.attackScenario:
1. Attacker sends malformed requests
2. Server returns detailed error messages
3. Information used for reconnaissance
4. Facilitates further attacks
highVulnerabilities.remediation: Sanitize error messages before displaying to users. Log detailed errors server-side only.
highVulnerabilities.codeExample:
// Instead of raw error.response?.data?.message:
const userFriendlyMessage = sanitizeErrorMessage(error);

mediumVulnerabilities.title: Insufficient Input Validation in Login Form
mediumVulnerabilities.description: Basic client-side validation only checks for empty fields, no password complexity or injection protection
mediumVulnerabilities.attackScenario:
1. User enters weak credentials
2. No complexity enforcement
3. Credentials vulnerable to brute force
4. Server-side validation bypassed if flawed
mediumVulnerabilities.remediation: Implement comprehensive client-side validation with server-side enforcement

mediumVulnerabilities.title: Role Authorization Logic Vulnerability
mediumVulnerabilities.description: Role hierarchy check may be vulnerable to role tampering if user object is compromised
mediumVulnerabilities.attackScenario:
1. Attacker modifies user.role in browser
2. Client-side role check passes
3. Unauthorized access to admin functions
4. Server validation bypassed if weak
mediumVulnerabilities.remediation: Always verify roles server-side. Client-side checks are for UX only.
mediumVulnerabilities.codeExample:
// Ensure server validates:
GET /api/v1/admin/users -> 401 if not admin role (verified server-side)

immediate.action: Replace localStorage token storage with httpOnly cookies

shortTerm.action: Implement proper session timeout with user consent
Add comprehensive input validation and sanitization
Implement secure error handling and logging

longTerm.action: Add rate limiting and brute force protection
Add session monitoring and anomaly detection

tokenStorage.recommended: httpOnly cookies with SameSite=Strict and Secure flags

csrfProtection.exemptEndpoints: Only GET requests for public data

securityHeaders.contentSecurityPolicy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' wss://your-domain.com

complianceNotes.kubernetesEnterprise: Current implementation fails enterprise security requirements due to CRITICAL vulnerabilities
complianceNotes.recommendations: Address all CRITICAL and HIGH severity issues before production deployment
complianceNotes.auditFrequency: Re-assess after implementation changes and quarterly thereafter
